content.prompt: Identify the leading term of these polynomials.

answer.worked:
The highest-power term in the numerator is $-2x^2$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Leading term}&=\frac{-2x^2}{4}\\&=-\frac12x^2\end{align*}$$

The highest-power term in the numerator is $x^3$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Leading term}&=\frac{x^3}{-7}\\&=-\frac{x^3}{7}\end{align*}$$

The highest-power term in the numerator is $x^3$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Leading term}&=\frac{x^3}{-8}\\&=-\frac{x^3}{8}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Leading term}&=x\times x\\&=x^2\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Leading term}&=-x\times x^2\\&=-x^3\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Leading term}&=2x\times x^2\times(-x)\\&=-2x^4\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Leading term}&=x^2\times(-x^3)\\&=-x^5\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Leading term}&=(2x^3)^3\\&=8x^9\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: These expressions are equivalent. By expanding and comparing coefficients, find the values of the pronumerals.

answer.worked:
Comparing coefficients gives $a-b=-1$ and $2a+b=7$. Adding these equations:

$$\begin{align*}3a&=6\\a&=2\end{align*}$$

Substituting into $a-b=-1$:

$$\begin{align*}2-b&=-1\\b&=3\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}a(x-1)^2+b(x-1)+c&=x^2\\a(x^2-2x+1)+bx-b+c&=x^2\\ax^2+(-2a+b)x+a-b+c&=x^2\end{align*}$$

Comparing coefficients:

$$\begin{align*}a&=1\\-2a+b&=0\\-2+b&=0\\b&=2\\a-b+c&=0\\1-2+c&=0\\c&=1\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: When multiplying two polynomials, $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$, the degree of the resulting product $P(x)Q(x)$ will be the sum of the degrees of $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$. Explain why this is true.

answer.short: The leading terms multiply, and their powers add. Their product has the highest power and a nonzero coefficient.
answer.worked: If the leading terms are $ax^m$ and $bx^n$, their product is $abx^{m+n}$ by the index law of multiplication. Since $a$ and $b$ are nonzero, $ab$ is nonzero. Every other product of terms has lower degree, so the degree of $P(x)Q(x)$ is $m+n$.

content.prompt: Consider $P(x)=ax^4+bx^3+cx^2+dx+e$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that if $P(x)$ is an even function, then $b=d=0$.

answer.worked:
For an even function, $P(-x)=P(x)$ for every $x$.
$$\begin{align*}P(-x)&=ax^4-bx^3+cx^2-dx+e\\ax^4-bx^3+cx^2-dx+e&=ax^4+bx^3+cx^2+dx+e\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients of $x^3$ and $x$ gives
$$\begin{align*}-b&=b\\b&=0\\-d&=d\\d&=0\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Using your result from part a, explain why for an even polynomial, if $x=\alpha$ is a root, then $x=-\alpha$ is also a root.

answer.worked:
From part a, $P(x)=ax^4+cx^2+e$. Since $\alpha$ is a root, $P(\alpha)=0$.
$$\begin{align*}P(-\alpha)&=a(-\alpha)^4+c(-\alpha)^2+e\\&=a\alpha^4+c\alpha^2+e\\&=P(\alpha)\\&=0\end{align*}$$
Hence $-\alpha$ is also a root.

For an odd function, $Q(-x)=-Q(x)$ for every $x$.
$$\begin{align*}Q(-x)&=-ax^5+bx^4-cx^3+dx^2-ex+f\\-Q(x)&=-ax^5-bx^4-cx^3-dx^2-ex-f\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients of $x^4$, $x^2$ and the constant terms gives
$$\begin{align*}b&=-b\\b&=0\\d&=-d\\d&=0\\f&=-f\\f&=0\end{align*}$$

From part a, only odd powers remain.
$$\begin{align*}Q(x)&=ax^5+cx^3+ex\\&=x(ax^4+cx^2+e)\\Q(0)&=0\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
1. Behaviour

$$\begin{align*}
\text{Leading term}&=(-x)(x)(-x)(-3x)(x)\\
&=-3x^5.
\end{align*}$$
As $x\to\infty$, $y\to-\infty$. The degree is odd, so as $x\to-\infty$, $y\to\infty$.

2. $y$-intercept

$$y=-(0)(-3)(2)(4)(2)=0.$$
The $y$-intercept is $(0,0)$.

3. $x$-intercepts

$$\begin{aligned}
x&=0,\quad x-3=0,\quad 2-x=0,\quad 4-3x=0,\quad x+2=0,\\
x&=-2,\ 0,\ \frac43,\ 2,\ 3.
\end{aligned}$$
Each factor occurs once, so the curve crosses the $x$-axis at every intercept. Sketch a smooth curve through these intercepts, with the left end upward and the right end downward.

children.prompt: Explain what happens to the curve at the $x$-intercept when there are repeated roots.

answer.short: Even multiplicity: the curve touches the axis and bounces. Odd multiplicity greater than $1$: it flattens and crosses the axis at a horizontal inflection.
answer.worked: Near a repeated root $x=a$, the repeated factor $(x-a)^m$ controls the local shape. When $m$ is even, its sign is the same on both sides, so the curve touches the axis and turns back. When $m$ is odd, its sign changes, so the curve crosses the axis. For odd multiplicity greater than $1$, the crossing is flattened with a horizontal inflection. Higher multiplicities give flatter contact with the axis.

answer.worked: The factor $(x+2)$ has exponent $1$, so $x=-2$ is a single root. The factor $(x-3)^2$ has exponent $2$, so $x=3$ is a double root.

$\begin{aligned}x+1&=0 &&\text{gives }x=-1\\x-3&=0 &&\text{gives }x=3\\x+5&=0 &&\text{gives }x=-5\end{aligned}$

Each linear factor has exponent $1$, so all three roots are single.
$x-5=0$ gives $x=5$. The factor has exponent $2$, so this is a double root.
$x+4=0$ gives $x=-4$. The factor has exponent $3$, so this is a triple root.

$\begin{aligned}x-2&=0 &&\text{gives }x=2\\x+4&=0 &&\text{gives }x=-4\end{aligned}$

The respective factor exponents are $2$ and $1$, so the roots are double and single.

$\begin{aligned}x+7&=0 &&\text{gives }x=-7\\x+3&=0 &&\text{gives }x=-3\end{aligned}$

The respective factor exponents are $3$ and $1$, so the roots are triple and single.

content.prompt: Consider the polynomial $P(x)=x^4-5x^2+4x+13$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: $P(x)$ can be expressed in the form $(x^2-a)^2+(x-b)^2$. Find the values of $a$ and $b$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}(x^2-a)^2+(x-b)^2&=x^4-2ax^2+a^2+x^2-2bx+b^2\\&=x^4+(1-2a)x^2-2bx+a^2+b^2.\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}1-2a&=-5\\a&=3\\-2b&=4\\b&=-2.\end{align*}$$
The constant term checks: $3^2+(-2)^2=13$. Thus $P(x)=(x^2-3)^2+(x+2)^2$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence explain why the graph of $P(x)$ has zero $x$-intercepts.

answer.short: Both squares are non-negative and cannot both be zero, so $P(x)>0$ for every real $x$. Hence there are no $x$-intercepts.
answer.worked: $P(x)=(x^2-3)^2+(x+2)^2$. Each square is non-negative. Their sum could be zero only if $x^2-3=0$ and $x+2=0$ simultaneously. However, $x+2=0$ gives $x=-2$, for which $x^2-3=1$. Therefore $P(x)>0$ for every real $x$, so its graph has no $x$-intercepts.

content.prompt:
Perform the following divisions and express each result in this form
$$\frac{P(x)}{D(x)}=Q(x)+\frac{R(x)}{D(x)}$$

answer.worked:
Divide the leading terms at each stage: $x^2\div x=x$, then $-5x\div x=-5$.
$$\begin{aligned}
(x^2-4x+1)-(x^2+x)&=-5x+1\\
(-5x+1)-(-5x-5)&=6\\
Q(x)&=x-5\\
R(x)&=6\\
\frac{x^2-4x+1}{x+1}&=x-5+\frac{6}{x+1}
\end{aligned}$$

Divide the leading terms at each stage: $x^2\div x=x$, then $-x\div x=-1$.
$$\begin{aligned}
(x^2-6x+5)-(x^2-5x)&=-x+5\\
(-x+5)-(-x+5)&=0\\
Q(x)&=x-1\\
R(x)&=0\\
\frac{x^2-6x+5}{x-5}&=x-1
\end{aligned}$$

content.prompt:
Consider the example $(4x^3+x-550)\div(x-5)$.

This polynomial is missing the $x^2$ term. When there are “gaps” in a polynomial, it is useful to insert any missing terms using a coefficient of $0$ so you can keep the terms lined up.

answer.worked:
Insert the missing term $0x^2$. Divide the leading terms, multiply by $x-5$ and subtract at each stage.
$$\begin{aligned}
(4x^3+0x^2+x-550)-(4x^3-20x^2)&=20x^2+x-550\\
(20x^2+x-550)-(20x^2-100x)&=101x-550\\
(101x-550)-(101x-505)&=-45.
\end{aligned}$$
The quotient terms are $4x^2$, $20x$ and $101$, so the blanks are $4x^2$ and $101$.
$$\frac{4x^3+x-550}{x-5}=4x^2+20x+101-\frac{45}{x-5}.$$

answer.worked:
Insert $0x^2$. Successive leading-term divisions give $x^2$, $2x$ and $-1$. Multiply each by $x-2$ and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}
(x^3+0x^2-5x+3)-(x^3-2x^2)&=2x^2-5x+3\\
(2x^2-5x+3)-(2x^2-4x)&=-x+3\\
(-x+3)-(-x+2)&=1.
\end{aligned}$$
$$\frac{x^3-5x+3}{x-2}=x^2+2x-1+\frac{1}{x-2}.$$

Insert $0x$. Successive leading-term divisions give $2x^2$, $-x$ and $1$. Multiply each by $x+1$ and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}
(2x^3+x^2+0x-11)-(2x^3+2x^2)&=-x^2-11\\
(-x^2+0x-11)-(-x^2-x)&=x-11\\
(x-11)-(x+1)&=-12.
\end{aligned}$$
$$\frac{2x^3+x^2-11}{x+1}=2x^2-x+1-\frac{12}{x+1}.$$

Insert $0x^2$ and $0x$. Successive leading-term divisions by $2x$ give $x^2$, $2x$ and $4$. Multiply each by $2x-4$ and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}
(2x^3+0x^2+0x-3)-(2x^3-4x^2)&=4x^2-3\\
(4x^2+0x-3)-(4x^2-8x)&=8x-3\\
(8x-3)-(8x-16)&=13.
\end{aligned}$$
$$\frac{2x^3-3}{2x-4}=x^2+2x+4+\frac{13}{2x-4}.$$

answer.worked:
Successive quotient terms:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{-2x^3}{x}&=-2x^2\\\frac{6x^2}{x}&=6x\\\frac{-29x}{x}&=-29\end{align*}$$
Subtract each divisor multiple:
$$\begin{align*}(-2x^3-2x^2-5x+7)-(-2x^3-8x^2)&=6x^2-5x+7\\(6x^2-5x+7)-(6x^2+24x)&=-29x+7\\(-29x+7)-(-29x-116)&=123\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\frac{-2x^3-2x^2-5x+7}{x+4}=-2x^2+6x-29+\frac{123}{x+4}.$$

Include the missing $x^2$ term as $0x^2$. Successive quotient terms:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x^3}{x}&=x^2\\\frac{2x^2}{x}&=2x\\\frac{-x}{x}&=-1\end{align*}$$
Subtract each divisor multiple:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+0x^2-5x+3)-(x^3-2x^2)&=2x^2-5x+3\\(2x^2-5x+3)-(2x^2-4x)&=-x+3\\(-x+3)-(-x+2)&=1\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\frac{x^3-5x+3}{x-2}=x^2+2x-1+\frac{1}{x-2}.$$

Include the missing $x^2$ term as $0x^2$. Successive quotient terms:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x^3}{x}&=x^2\\\frac{-x^2}{x}&=-x\\\frac{-2x}{x}&=-2\end{align*}$$
Subtract each divisor multiple:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+0x^2-3x-2)-(x^3+x^2)&=-x^2-3x-2\\(-x^2-3x-2)-(-x^2-x)&=-2x-2\\(-2x-2)-(-2x-2)&=0\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\frac{x^3-3x-2}{x+1}=x^2-x-2.$$

answer.worked:
Divide the leading terms: $x^3\div x^2=x$. Multiply and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}(x^3-3x^2+3x-1)-x(x^2+5)&=-3x^2-2x-1.\end{aligned}$$
Next, $-3x^2\div x^2=-3$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(-3x^2-2x-1)-(-3)(x^2+5)=-2x+14.$$
The remainder has degree less than 2, so
$$\frac{x^3-3x^2+3x-1}{x^2+5}=x-3+\frac{-2x+14}{x^2+5}.$$

Divide the leading terms: $2x^3\div x^2=2x$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(2x^3+4x^2-x+8)-2x(x^2+3x+2)=-2x^2-5x+8.$$
Next, $-2x^2\div x^2=-2$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(-2x^2-5x+8)-(-2)(x^2+3x+2)=x+12.$$
The remainder has degree less than 2, so
$$\frac{2x^3+4x^2-x+8}{x^2+3x+2}=2x-2+\frac{x+12}{x^2+3x+2}.$$

Divide the leading terms: $2x^4\div x^2=2x^2$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(2x^4-5x^3+2x^2+2x-5)-2x^2(x^2-2x)=-x^3+2x^2+2x-5.$$
Next, $-x^3\div x^2=-x$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(-x^3+2x^2+2x-5)-(-x)(x^2-2x)=2x-5.$$
The remainder has degree less than 2, so
$$\frac{2x^4-5x^3+2x^2+2x-5}{x^2-2x}=2x^2-x+\frac{2x-5}{x^2-2x}.$$

Write the dividend as $x^5+0x^4+x^3+5x^2-6x+15$ to keep powers aligned. Divide the leading terms: $x^5\div x^2=x^3$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(x^5+x^3+5x^2-6x+15)-x^3(x^2+3)=-2x^3+5x^2-6x+15.$$
Next, $-2x^3\div x^2=-2x$. Multiply and subtract:
$$(-2x^3+5x^2-6x+15)-(-2x)(x^2+3)=5x^2+15.$$
Finally, $5x^2\div x^2=5$, and
$$(5x^2+15)-5(x^2+3)=0.$$
The remainder is zero, so
$$\frac{x^5+x^3+5x^2-6x+15}{x^2+3}=x^3-2x+5.$$

sourceReview.taughtMethod: Multiply the division identity by the divisor to obtain the quotient-remainder form.

answer.worked:
Multiply every term by $x+2$:
$$\color{#268cff}{\begin{aligned}x^3-x^2+x-1&=(x^2-3x+7)(x+2)-15.\end{aligned}}$$

Multiply every term by $x+1$:
$$\color{#268cff}{\begin{aligned}x^2-5x+3&=(x-6)(x+1)+9.\end{aligned}}$$

Use polynomial long division by $x+3$.
First, $2x^3\div x=2x^2$. Multiply and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}(2x^3-x^2+3x-1)-(2x^3+6x^2)&=-7x^2+3x-1.\end{aligned}$$
Next, $-7x^2\div x=-7x$. Multiply and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}(-7x^2+3x-1)-(-7x^2-21x)&=24x-1.\end{aligned}$$
Finally, $24x\div x=24$. Multiply and subtract:
$$\begin{aligned}(24x-1)-(24x+72)&=-73.\end{aligned}$$
The quotient is $2x^2-7x+24$ and the remainder is $-73$, so
$$\color{#268cff}{2x^3-x^2+3x-1=(x+3)(2x^2-7x+24)-73.}$$

content.prompt: Divide these polynomials and write in the form $P(x)=D(x)Q(x)+R(x)$.

answer.worked:
Long division gives quotient terms $x^2$ and $2x$:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+x^2-2x+3)-x^2(x-1)&=2x^2-2x+3\\(2x^2-2x+3)-2x(x-1)&=3\\Q(x)&=x^2+2x\\R(x)&=3\\x^3+x^2-2x+3&=(x-1)(x^2+2x)+3\end{align*}$$

Include $0x^2$ in the dividend. Long division gives quotient terms $x^2$, $-2x$ and $3$:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+0x^2-x+1)-x^2(x+2)&=-2x^2-x+1\\(-2x^2-x+1)-(-2x)(x+2)&=3x+1\\(3x+1)-3(x+2)&=-5\\Q(x)&=x^2-2x+3\\R(x)&=-5\\x^3-x+1&=(x+2)(x^2-2x+3)-5\end{align*}$$

Include $0x$ in the dividend. Long division gives quotient terms $x^2$, $2x$ and $2$:
$$\begin{align*}(x^3+x^2+0x-3)-x^2(x-1)&=2x^2-3\\(2x^2+0x-3)-2x(x-1)&=2x-3\\(2x-3)-2(x-1)&=-1\\Q(x)&=x^2+2x+2\\R(x)&=-1\\x^3+x^2-3&=(x-1)(x^2+2x+2)-1\end{align*}$$

Include the missing terms with zero coefficients. Long division gives quotient terms $x^3$, $4x^2$, $15x$ and $60$:
$$\begin{align*}(x^4+0x^3-x^2+0x+0)-x^3(x-4)&=4x^3-x^2\\(4x^3-x^2+0x+0)-4x^2(x-4)&=15x^2\\(15x^2+0x+0)-15x(x-4)&=60x\\60x-60(x-4)&=240\\Q(x)&=x^3+4x^2+15x+60\\R(x)&=240\\x^4-x^2&=(x-4)(x^3+4x^2+15x+60)+240\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Continue the supplied long division:
$$\begin{aligned}(3x^4-4x^3+0x^2+4x-8)-(3x^4-6x^2)&=-4x^3+6x^2+4x-8,\\(-4x^3+6x^2+4x-8)-(-4x^3+8x)&=6x^2-4x-8,\\(6x^2-4x-8)-(6x^2-12)&=-4x+4.\end{aligned}$$
The quotient terms are $3x^2$, $-4x$ and $6$.
$$\begin{aligned}3x^4-4x^3+4x-8&=(x^2-2)(3x^2-4x+6)\\&\quad-4x+4.\end{aligned}$$

Long division gives quotient terms $x$ and $-2$:
$$\begin{aligned}(x^3-3x^2+x+4)-(x^3-x^2)&=-2x^2+x+4,\\(-2x^2+x+4)-(-2x^2+2x)&=-x+4.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}x^3-3x^2+x+4&=(x^2-x)(x-2)\\&\quad-x+4.\end{aligned}$$

Long division gives quotient terms $x$ and $-2$:
$$\begin{aligned}(x^3+x^2-7x+6)-(x^3+3x^2-x)&=-2x^2-6x+6,\\(-2x^2-6x+6)-(-2x^2-6x+2)&=4.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}x^3+x^2-7x+6&=(x^2+3x-1)(x-2)\\&\quad+4.\end{aligned}$$

Long division gives quotient terms $x^2$, $x$ and $3$:
$$\begin{aligned}(x^4-3x^3+x^2-7x+3)-(x^4-4x^3+2x^2)&=x^3-x^2-7x+3,\\(x^3-x^2-7x+3)-(x^3-4x^2+2x)&=3x^2-9x+3,\\(3x^2-9x+3)-(3x^2-12x+6)&=3x-3.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}x^4-3x^3+x^2-7x+3&=(x^2-4x+2)(x^2+x+3)\\&\quad+3x-3.\end{aligned}$$

Long division gives quotient terms $x$ and $-3$:
$$\begin{aligned}(x^3-3x^2+5x-4)-(x^3+2x)&=-3x^2+3x-4,\\(-3x^2+3x-4)-(-3x^2-6)&=3x+2.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}x^3-3x^2+5x-4&=(x^2+2)(x-3)\\&\quad+3x+2.\end{aligned}$$

Include the missing $x^2$ and $x$ terms. Long division gives quotient terms $x^2$, $2x$ and $4$:
$$\begin{aligned}(2x^3+0x^2+0x-3)-(2x^3-4x^2)&=4x^2-3,\\(4x^2+0x-3)-(4x^2-8x)&=8x-3,\\(8x-3)-(8x-16)&=13.\end{aligned}$$
$$2x^3-3=(2x-4)(x^2+2x+4)+13.$$

content.prompt: If $x^4-2x^3-20x^2+mx+n$ is exactly divisible by $x^2-5x+2$, find $m$ and $n$.

answer.short: $m=41$, $n=-14$. Long division gives remainder $(m-41)x+(n+14)$; exact divisibility requires both coefficients to be zero.
answer.worked:
The successive quotient terms in long division are $x^2$, $3x$ and $-7$.
$$\begin{aligned}
(x^4-2x^3-20x^2+mx+n)-x^2(x^2-5x+2)&=3x^3-22x^2+mx+n\\
(3x^3-22x^2+mx+n)-3x(x^2-5x+2)&=-7x^2+(m-6)x+n\\
(-7x^2+(m-6)x+n)-(-7)(x^2-5x+2)&=(m-41)x+(n+14).
\end{aligned}$$
Thus
$$\begin{aligned}
x^4-2x^3-20x^2+mx+n&=(x^2-5x+2)(x^2+3x-7)\\
&\quad +(m-41)x+(n+14).
\end{aligned}$$
Exact divisibility means the remainder is zero, so
$$\begin{aligned}
m-41&=0\\
n+14&=0\\
m&=41,\qquad n=-14.
\end{aligned}$$

Find $a$ and $b$ given that $(x+2)$ is a factor of $P(x)$,
and $-24$ is the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $x-1$.

answer.worked:
By the factor theorem, $P(-2)=0$.
$$\begin{align*}P(-2)&=(-2)^3+a(-2)^2+b(-2)-18,\\0&=-8+4a-2b-18,\\4a-2b&=26.\end{align*}$$
By the remainder theorem, $P(1)=-24$.
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1+a+b-18,\\-24&=a+b-17,\\a+b&=-7.\end{align*}$$
Adding twice the second equation to the first:
$$\begin{align*}6a&=12,\\a&=2,\\b&=-7-2=-9.\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
The polynomial $P(x)$ is divided by $(x+4)(x-3)$.
Find the remainder if $P(-4)=11$ and $P(3)=-3$.

answer.short: $R(x)=3-2x$. Write $R(x)=ax+b$ and use the divisor's roots.
answer.worked:
The divisor has degree 2, so write the remainder as $ax+b$.
$$P(x)=(x+4)(x-3)Q(x)+ax+b.$$
$$\begin{align*}P(-4)&=-4a+b=11,\\P(3)&=3a+b=-3.\end{align*}$$
Subtracting the first equation from the second:
$$\begin{align*}7a&=-14,\\a&=-2.\end{align*}$$
Substituting into $3a+b=-3$:
$$\begin{align*}3(-2)+b&=-3,\\b&=3,\\R(x)&=3-2x.\end{align*}$$

By the factor theorem, $P(1)=0$ and $P(2)=0$.
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1+m+n=0,\\m+n&=-1,\\P(2)&=16+2m+n=0,\\2m+n&=-16.\end{align*}$$
Subtracting $m+n=-1$ from $2m+n=-16$:
$$\begin{align*}m&=-15,\\n&=-1-(-15)=14.\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
When a polynomial is divided by $(2x+1)(x-3)$, the remainder is $3x-1$.
What is the remainder when the polynomial is divided by $2x+1$?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(2x+1)(x-3)Q(x)+(3x-1)\\P\left(-\frac12\right)&=\left(2\left(-\frac12\right)+1\right)\left(-\frac12-3\right)Q\left(-\frac12\right)+3\left(-\frac12\right)-1\\P\left(-\frac12\right)&=-\frac32-1\\P\left(-\frac12\right)&=-\frac52\end{align*}$$
By the remainder theorem, the remainder is $-\frac52$.

content.prompt: Factorise these polynomials, and hence solve $P(x)=0$.

answer.worked:
Test integer factors of $6$.
$$P(-1)=-1-4-1+6=0.$$
Therefore $x+1$ is a factor. Use polynomial long division:
$$\begin{aligned}P(x)-x^2(x+1)&=-5x^2+x+6\\(-5x^2+x+6)-(-5x)(x+1)&=6x+6\\(6x+6)-6(x+1)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The quotient is $x^2-5x+6$.
$$P(x)=(x+1)(x^2-5x+6)=(x+1)(x-2)(x-3).$$
Using the null factor law, $x=-1,2,3$.

Test integer factors of $30$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(1)&=1+6-1-30=-24\\P(2)&=8+24-2-30=0.\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $x-2$ is a factor. Use polynomial long division:
$$\begin{aligned}P(x)-x^2(x-2)&=8x^2-x-30\\(8x^2-x-30)-8x(x-2)&=15x-30\\(15x-30)-15(x-2)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The quotient is $x^2+8x+15$.
$$P(x)=(x-2)(x^2+8x+15)=(x-2)(x+3)(x+5).$$
Using the null factor law, $x=-5,-3,2$.

Test integer factors of $10$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(1)&=2-13+13+10=12\\P(-1)&=-2-13-13+10=-18\\P(2)&=16-52+26+10=0.\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $x-2$ is a factor. Use polynomial long division:
$$\begin{aligned}P(x)-2x^2(x-2)&=-9x^2+13x+10\\(-9x^2+13x+10)-(-9x)(x-2)&=-5x+10\\(-5x+10)-(-5)(x-2)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The quotient is $2x^2-9x-5$.
$$\begin{aligned}2x^2-9x-5&=2x^2-10x+x-5\\&=(2x+1)(x-5).\end{aligned}$$
Hence $P(x)=(x-2)(2x+1)(x-5)$. Using the null factor law, $x=-\frac12,2,5$.

Test integer factors of $5$.
$$P(1)=1+4-5=0.$$
Therefore $x-1$ is a factor. Use polynomial long division, including the zero coefficient of $x^2$:
$$\begin{aligned}P(x)-x^2(x-1)&=x^2+4x-5\\(x^2+4x-5)-x(x-1)&=5x-5\\(5x-5)-5(x-1)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
Hence $P(x)=(x-1)(x^2+x+5)$. By the null factor law, $x=1$ or $x^2+x+5=0$. The quadratic has discriminant $1^2-4(1)(5)=-19<0$, so it has no real roots. Therefore $x=1$ is the only real solution.

inlines.text: For each of the following cubic equations, follow these steps.
Use the factor theorem to find a factor.
Use long division to find the quotient.
Write the polynomial in a fully factorised form.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^3-4x^2+x+6$. Test factors of $6$: $P(-1)=-1-4-1+6=0$, so $x+1$ is a factor. Long division, subtracting each product row, gives
$$\begin{array}{rrrrr}&x^2&-5x&+6&\\\hline x+1&x^3&-4x^2&+x&+6\\&x^3&+x^2&&\\\hline &&-5x^2&+x&+6\\&&-5x^2&-5x&\\\hline &&&6x&+6\\&&&6x&+6\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+1)(x^2-5x+6)\\&=(x+1)(x-2)(x-3).\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=-1,\ 2,\ 3$.

Let $P(x)=x^3-6x^2+11x-6$. Test factors of $-6$: $P(1)=1-6+11-6=0$, so $x-1$ is a factor. Long division, subtracting each product row, gives
$$\begin{array}{rrrrr}&x^2&-5x&+6&\\\hline x-1&x^3&-6x^2&+11x&-6\\&x^3&-x^2&&\\\hline &&-5x^2&+11x&-6\\&&-5x^2&+5x&\\\hline &&&6x&-6\\&&&6x&-6\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-1)(x^2-5x+6)\\&=(x-1)(x-2)(x-3).\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=1,\ 2,\ 3$.

Let $P(x)=x^3-3x^2-16x-12$. Test factors of $-12$: $P(-1)=-1-3+16-12=0$, so $x+1$ is a factor. Long division, subtracting each product row, gives
$$\begin{array}{rrrrr}&x^2&-4x&-12&\\\hline x+1&x^3&-3x^2&-16x&-12\\&x^3&+x^2&&\\\hline &&-4x^2&-16x&-12\\&&-4x^2&-4x&\\\hline &&&-12x&-12\\&&&-12x&-12\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+1)(x^2-4x-12)\\&=(x+1)(x+2)(x-6).\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=-2,\ -1,\ 6$.

Rearrange to $2x^3-3x^2-11x+6=0$. Let $P(x)=2x^3-3x^2-11x+6$. Test factors of $6$: $P(-2)=-16-12+22+6=0$, so $x+2$ is a factor. Long division, subtracting each product row, gives
$$\begin{array}{rrrrr}&2x^2&-7x&+3&\\\hline x+2&2x^3&-3x^2&-11x&+6\\&2x^3&+4x^2&&\\\hline &&-7x^2&-11x&+6\\&&-7x^2&-14x&\\\hline &&&3x&+6\\&&&3x&+6\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+2)(2x^2-7x+3)\\&=(x+2)(2x-1)(x-3).\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=-2,\ \frac12,\ 3$.

answer.worked:
$$2(x^3-7x^2+7x+15)=0.$$

$$3(x^3+4x^2+x-6)=0.$$

content.prompt: Explain why $x^4+x^2=0$ has only one real solution.

answer.short: $x^2(x^2+1)=0$. Since $x^2+1>0$ for real $x$, the only real solution is $x=0$.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}x^4+x^2&=0\\x^2(x^2+1)&=0\end{align*}$$ By the null factor law, $x^2=0$ or $x^2+1=0$. The first gives $x=0$. For the second, $$\begin{align*}x^2+1&=0\\x^2&=-1\end{align*}$$ A real square cannot be negative, so this gives no real solution. Therefore the only real solution is $x=0$.

content.prompt: Show that $P(x)=x^3+x+3$ does not have an integer zero by testing all the possible integer zeros.

answer.short: $P(-3)=-27$, $P(-1)=1$, $P(1)=5$, $P(3)=33$. None is zero, so there is no integer zero.
answer.worked:
Any integer zero must be a factor of $3$, so test $-3,-1,1,3$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(-3)&=(-3)^3+(-3)+3=-27\\P(-1)&=(-1)^3+(-1)+3=1\\P(1)&=1^3+1+3=5\\P(3)&=3^3+3+3=33\end{aligned}$$
None of the possible integer zeros gives $P(x)=0$. Therefore $P(x)$ has no integer zero.

content.prompt: Use the quadratic formula to solve for $x$, expressing your answers in exact form.

answer.worked:
By the null factor law, $x=1$ or $x^2-2x-4=0$. For the quadratic:
$$\begin{aligned}x&=\frac{-(-2)\pm\sqrt{(-2)^2-4(1)(-4)}}{2(1)}\\x&=\frac{2\pm\sqrt{20}}2\\x&=1\pm\sqrt5\end{aligned}$$

The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $(-5,0)$, $(-3,0)$, $(3,0)$ and $(5,0)$, and the $y$-axis at $(0,225)$. Each root is simple, so the curve crosses at each intercept. Only even powers occur, so the graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis. The positive quartic leading term means both ends rise.

content.prompt: Factorise $x^4-x^3-5x^2+12$.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^4-x^3-5x^2+12$. Test an integer factor of $12$:
$$\begin{aligned}P(2)&=16-8-20+12\\&=0.\end{aligned}$$
So $x-2$ is a factor. Polynomial long division gives
$$\begin{array}{r|rrrr} &x^3&+x^2&-3x&-6\\\hline x-2&x^4&-x^3&-5x^2&+0x+12\\ &x^4&-2x^3&&\\\hline &&x^3&-5x^2&+0x+12\\ &&x^3&-2x^2&\\\hline &&&-3x^2&+0x+12\\ &&&-3x^2&+6x\\\hline &&&&-6x+12\\ &&&&-6x+12\\\hline &&&&0\end{array}$$
For $Q(x)=x^3+x^2-3x-6$,
$$\begin{aligned}Q(2)&=8+4-6-6\\&=0.\end{aligned}$$
Thus $x-2$ is also a factor of $Q(x)$. Dividing again:
$$\begin{array}{r|rrr} &x^2&+3x&+3\\\hline x-2&x^3&+x^2&-3x-6\\ &x^3&-2x^2&\\\hline &&3x^2&-3x-6\\ &&3x^2&-6x\\\hline &&&3x-6\\ &&&3x-6\\\hline &&&0\end{array}$$
$$\begin{aligned}P(x)&=(x-2)(x^3+x^2-3x-6)\\&=(x-2)^2(x^2+3x+3).\end{aligned}$$

spec.mathematics: The cube's side elevation is a unit square. The ladder joins (0,H) to (D,0), where H≈9.93799368936 and D≈1.11188193176, with H²+D²=100 and 1/H+1/D=1, so it passes through (1,1).

answer.short: Similar triangles give $y=\frac1x$. Substituting into $(x+1)^2+(y+1)^2=100$ gives $x^4+2x^3-98x^2+2x+1=0$.
answer.worked:
Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)^2+(1+y)^2&=10^2.\end{align*}$$
Using similar triangles:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{y}{1}&=\frac{1}{x}\\y&=\frac{1}{x}.\end{align*}$$
Substitute, expand and multiply every term by $x^2$:
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)^2+\left(1+\frac1x\right)^2&=100\\x^2+2x+2+\frac2x+\frac1{x^2}&=100\\x^4+2x^3+2x^2+2x+1&=100x^2\\x^4+2x^3-98x^2+2x+1&=0.\end{align*}$$

entries.description:
A polynomial in factored form is P(x) = k(x − a)(x − b)(x − c)(x − d) …
The x-intercepts are at x = a, b, c, d …

3. Determine the x-intercepts by letting y = 0 (use null-factor law).

entries.description:
Sketching Polynomials with Roots of Multiplicity
1. Determine curve behaviour at x → ∞ (identify leading coefficient).
• If leading coefficient is positive, then x → ∞, y → ∞.
• If leading coefficient is negative, then x → ∞, y → −∞.
2. Determine the y-intercept by letting x = 0 (multiply constant terms in each factor).
3. Determine the x-intercepts by letting y = 0 (use null-factor law).
4. Identify the behaviour of the curve at the x-intercepts.

entries.description:
We will apply this idea to polynomials:
Last lesson we used polynomial division to show that, given a dividend P(x), divisor D(x), quotient Q(x), and remainder R(x):
P(x)/D(x) = Q(x) + R(x)/D(x).
We multiply every term by D(x) to derive the quotient-remainder form of a polynomial:
P(x) = Q(x)D(x) + R(x).
Two important facts:
• The degree of the remainder is always less than the divisor: deg R(x) < deg D(x).
• When R(x) = 0, then Q(x) and D(x) are factors of P(x): P(x) = Q(x) × D(x).

entries.expectedAnswer:
Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
(x + 1)^2 + (1 + y)^2 = 10^2
Using similar triangles, y/1 = 1/x

(x + 1)^2 + (1 + 1/x)^2 = 10^2
Expand, multiply every term by x^2, then rearrange.
x^4 + 2x^3 − 98x^2 + 2x + 1 = 0
